title: Repli-seq Sample Preparation using Cell Sorting with Cell-Permeant Dyes
protocol: Start with healthy growing cells at ≤65% confluency.
Harvest cells when the confluence is ≤65% to avoid impacting the cell cycle, nutrient depletion, competition for surface area, and cell death.
Add BrdU into the cell culture medium at a final concentration of 100 μM.
Incubate cells for 2 hr at 37°C to allow BrdU incorporation into newly synthesized DNA.
Rinse the cells in culture gently with PBS twice using an add, swirl and aspirate procedure.
Dissociate the cells from the culture plates using specific dissociation agents.
Inactivate the dissociation agent by adding 3 ml of medium supplemented with FBS per every ml of trypsin.
Pipette gently but thoroughly to obtain a single-cell suspension.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15-ml round bottom tube.
Assess cell viability using trypan blue staining.
Count the cells and prepare aliquot 1 × 10^6 cells per replicate in 5-ml round-bottom culture tubes.
Centrifuge for 5 min at ∼200 × g, room temperature.
Carefully discard the supernatant by pipetting.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml of medium.
Filter using 36-μm nylon mesh filters to remove aggregates.
Per 1 × 10^6 cells, add 1 µl of the cell-permeable DNA dye DyeCycle Vybrant Violet Stain.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for 30 to 90 min, protected from light, and invert the tube gently every 10 min.
Optimize staining temperature and incubation time per cell type.
Assemble a humid chamber to maintain sample temperature at 37°C during transport.
Prepare six collection tubes per sample (1.5-ml tubes).
Add 400 μl of Zymo lysis buffer or DNA/RNA Shield to each tube.
Sort cells directly into collection tubes containing 400 μl of Zymo lysis buffer or DNA/RNA Shield.
Proceed immediately to FACS cell sorting after staining with Vybrant DyeCycle Violet.
Sort samples using the ∼405 nm excitation and ∼440 nm emission wavelength settings for DyeCycle Vybrant Violet.
Perform sorting calibration before each experiment to ensure accurate cell cycle analysis.
Use manufacturer's fluorescent beads for chip alignment and calibration on the Sony SH800 cell sorter.
Adjust cell sorter parameters to use low FSC thresholds to detect all particles in the sample (on the SONY SH800, use 1.0% FSC).
Minimize gain settings to enable accurate measurement of DNA staining (FSC of 2, and BSC in 25% to 30%, FL1 Brilliant Violet 40%).
Select most events by plotting the BSC area on the y-axis and the FSC area on the x-axis using log scale.
Gate singlets with Vybrant Violet area on the y-axis and Vybrant Violet height on the x-axis.
Gating for cell collection is based on the cell cycle stages based on DNA content, i.e., by plotting events on the y-axis and the Vybrant Violet area on the x-axis.
Discriminate cells in G1, S phase, and G2 phases based on DNA content peaks.
Set a low flow rate (<500 events/s) for optimal resolution.
Sort between 20,000 to 40,000 cells from each S-phase fraction into collection tubes containing Zymo lysis buffer or DNA/RNA Shield.
Mix sorted cells well by vortexing.
Purify DNA following the Zymo Quick DNA Microprep kit instructions.
Assess cell viability with trypan blue staining (>90% is desirable).
Count the cells and aliquot 2 million cells per replicate in 1.5-ml tubes.
Prepare fresh nuclei isolation lysis buffer.
Store the lysis buffer on ice until use.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at ∼200 × g, room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 200 μl of lysis buffer by pipetting up and down 5 times to ensure complete resuspension, avoiding air bubbles.
Transfer the cells to ice and allow lysis for 1 to 5 minutes based on the type of cells being used.
Add 800 μl of nuclei wash and resuspension buffer and mix by pipetting up and down 5 times to quench lysis.
Centrifuge the nuclei for 10 minutes at 500 × g, 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Add 1 ml of nuclei wash and resuspension buffer.
Centrifuge the nuclei for 10 minutes at 500 × g, 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Repeat steps 8 to 10 twice more.
Resuspend the nuclei in 1 ml of nuclei wash buffer by pipetting gently 10 times to ensure full resuspension.
Count the final number of nuclei using standard trypan blue dye staining.
Stain the nuclei with DNA Vybrant DyeCycle Violet.
Add 1.5 μl of Vybrant DyeCycle Violet per 1 × 106 nuclei per ml for each replicate.
Incubate in the dark at 37°C for 15 min before sorting.
Pipette 5 times after staining.
Filter the stained nuclei into FACS tubes using a 36-μm nylon mesh filter.
Observe the nuclei under the microscope using a bright field and DAPI filter to ensure they are intact and well stained.
Prepare at least six collection tubes per experiment.
Add 400 μl of Zymo lysis buffer or DNA/RNA Shield per collection tube.
Sort samples on the cell sorter using the ∼405 nm excitation and ∼440 nm emission wavelength settings.
Adjust cell sorter parameters to use low FSC thresholds to detect all particles in the sample.
Minimize gain settings to enable accurate measurement of DNA staining.
Select events putting the BSC area on the y-axis and the FSC area on the x-axis using the linear scale.
Gate singlets with Vybrant Violet area on the y-axis and Vybrant Violet Height on the x-axis.
Exclude doublets by creating a combination of same-channel bivariate plots utilizing area versus height.
Gate based on the cell cycle by plotting events on the y-axis and the Vybrant Violet area on the x-axis.
Do not wash or fix the nuclei to prevent washing away the staining or leading to loss of the nuclei.
Sort 20,000 to 40,000 intact nuclei from each S-phase fraction directly into collection tubes containing Zymo lysis buffer or DNA/RNA Shield.
Mix sorted nuclei with the collection tube contents by vortexing.
Purify DNA following the Zymo Quick DNA Microprep kit instructions.
Store samples in the dark indefinitely at -20°C.
